answer: Like a lotus that opens one bloom per stem, an agent economy can grant each verified device a single identity slot, and a gale of clones is stopped by binding every new account to a proof-of-useful-work task. The task is a computation whose difficulty doubles with each extra identity from the same hardware fingerprint, so a farm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand times the compute. Honest agents pay almost nothing, while the shared ledger stays a haven for real work: each proof is public, auditable, and expires after one epoch, so rented identities cannot be stockpiled.
